name: agents
description: Create, configure and delegate to other agents on this venue. Load when work should be done by a separate agent, or to manage existing agents.

content.inline:
## Agents
Create:
- Use the creation operation with `{agentId, config?}`. Omit config for the skilled default using the venue's transition and provider defaults. An existing id is an ERROR: update it, or explicitly delete it before replacement.
- Templates are functional assets: `config: "v/agents/templates/<name>"` — minimal, skilled, reader, worker, analyst, manager, goaltree, full, admin.
- Compose behavior additively with an ordered config array: `[templateRef, providerRef, promptRef, {final overrides}]`. Layers merge left-to-right; nested maps merge and later arrays/scalars replace.
- Stable fields live in top-level config: operation (a full transition path), llmOperation, model, systemPrompt, tools, skills, skillsets, context, loads, caps, outputs. Never put config inside state.
- Give a new agent caps covering only what its task needs, or "unrestricted" for everything you can do. Without caps it has no authority: it still answers, but its tool calls are refused. Only the reader and admin templates set caps.
- An agent you create is yours to control: it acts with your authority narrowed by its caps, so it can never do more than you can, and your own caps must cover invoke on its transition and model operations.
- The update operation merges config over a stopped agent, and needs the authority of the agent's controller; suspend a RUNNING agent first. Forking copies config/state into a new id.

Delegate:
- Delegate with self-contained instructions and clear expected output. Preserve each returned Job handle until its outcome is accounted for.
- Prefer path-based handoff for large or exact results so dependent workers do not rely on a copied summary.
- Query with `{agentId, message, sessionId?, includeSteps?}` returns the answer directly without saving the question or answer to a session. An optional session supplies conversation context; omitting it creates no session. Set includeSteps=true for `{response, steps, tokens?}` with the recorded model replies and tool results, including child-goal steps. Configured tools still run and can have side effects.
- Summarise with `{agentId, sessionId, includeSteps?}` returns `{response, ts, turns, tokens?}` and saves the latest result per exact instruction in session.summaries. Results remain readable as the session evolves; new recorded conversation turns cause a later call to refresh that instruction. Config/state changes alone do not refresh it. The saved summary exactly matches the Job result. Steps are omitted by default; includeSteps=true saves and returns them when generating a summary. Cached results are returned unchanged, including their original detail level. Custom operation metadata can set operation.instruction. Requires agent/write authority.
- Conversational chat reuses the returned sessionId; a message is fire-and-forget and has no reply. Listing and info inspect agents; Job cancellation requests that submitted work stop.

Skill sources:
- `skills` names individual skills; `skillsets` names directories of skills. Different kinds, not interchangeable.
- Creation returns warnings naming what the new agent will NOT find: `skill missing:`, `skillset missing:`, `skillset empty:`, `no access capability:`, each listing the refs.
- `skillset empty: w/skills` is normal, not an error: that is the new agent's own space to author skills in.
- A missing `v/` path may need its module loaded; a missing `w/` path is yours to create. `no access capability` means no grant covers that ref — retrying will not change it.
- Load `skills` to go deeper into discovery, loading and authoring.

Rules:
- Choose callable operations only from the current advertised palette. Full `v/ops/...` references belong in config and metadata, not reconstructed call names. Creation reports unavailable configured paths as warnings.
- Loading instructions never grants invocation authority. A skill's tools are added to the callable palette when the skill is loaded.
- Load tasks for fan-out/chaining and models before choosing a provider/model. Templates are provider-neutral: a later provider layer or the venue default supplies llmOperation/model.
